# War Scroll Column 11 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in War Scroll Column 11 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 11:1 — "terrible" vs. "awe-inspiring" — divine epithet register

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "terri[ble] God" | Preserves traditional biblical register and the manuscript's partial lacuna |
| LOGOS | "terri[ble] God" | Standard rendering following Yadin's edition |
| PNEUMA | "awe-inspiring God" | Modern English avoids misreading "terrible" as pejorative |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "terri[ble] God" (EMET/LOGOS). The lacuna is genuine and must be marked; "terrible" in biblical register means "causing terror/awe," which is contextually correct.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 11:2 — "mighty men" vs. "the powerful" — military terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "mighty-men" | Hyphenated construct preserving Hebrew gibborim |
| LOGOS | "mighty men" | Standard biblical English for gibborim |
| PNEUMA | "the powerful" | Generic modern English rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "mighty men" (LOGOS). Preserves the biblical military register without EMET's hyphenation or PNEUMA's abstraction.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 11:2-3 — "angelic host" vs. "Heaven's fiercest warriors" — celestial army designation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "warriors of-the-angelic-host" | Literal with construct chain |
| LOGOS | "Valiant warriors of the angelic host" | Formal English with "angelic host" as standard DSS term |
| PNEUMA | "Heaven's fiercest warriors" | Dynamic rendering emphasizing martial prowess |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Valiant warriors of the angelic host" (LOGOS). "Angelic host" is the established scholarly rendering; "Heaven's fiercest warriors" loses the technical sectarian designation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 11:3 — "Hero of War" vs. "Divine Warrior" — divine epithet

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Hero-of-War" | Literal rendering of gibbor milchamah |
| LOGOS | "Hero of War" | Formal equivalent preserving the Hebrew epithet |
| PNEUMA | "Divine Warrior" | Interpretive rendering identifying the figure as God |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Hero of War" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew gibbor milchamah is a specific epithet; "Divine Warrior" imports interpretation not explicit in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 11:3-4 — "horsemen" vs. "cavalry" — military unit designation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "horsemen" | Literal translation of parashim |
| LOGOS | "horsemen" | Standard rendering |
| PNEUMA | "cavalry" | Modern military equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "horsemen" (EMET/LOGOS). Biblical military vocabulary preserved.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 11:4 — "dew-mist" vs. "morning dew" — meteorological imagery

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "dew-mist" | Literal compound rendering of Hebrew tal |
| LOGOS | "mist of dew" | Formal English inversion |
| PNEUMA | "morning dew" | Added "morning" for English idiom |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "mist of dew" (LOGOS). More readable than EMET's hyphenation; PNEUMA adds "morning" without textual warrant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 11:4 — "showering justice" vs. "drenching the ground with justice" — imagery

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "showering justice upon-all her-growth" | Literal, preserving Hebrew imagery |
| LOGOS | "pouring out justice upon all that grows from her" | Formal expansion |
| PNEUMA | "drenching the ground with justice wherever life grows" | Dynamic expansion with added "life" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "showering justice upon all her growth" (close to EMET). Concise and faithful; PNEUMA's "drenching" and "life" add without warrant.

**Status:** Resolved with EMET base, minor adjustment.

---

## 11:6 — "Torah" vs. "God's instruction" — key term

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "instructed in-the-Torah" | Preserves Hebrew term |
| LOGOS | "learned in the Torah" | Preserves Hebrew term with different English verb |
| PNEUMA | "trained in God's instruction" | Translates Torah as "God's instruction" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "instructed in the Torah" (EMET). Torah is a universally recognized term that should be preserved untranslated per project conventions.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 11:7 — "Honored One" vs. "Glorious One" — divine title

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-Honored-One" | Rendering of nikhbad |
| LOGOS | "the Honored One" | Same rendering, unhyphenated |
| PNEUMA | "the Glorious One" | Alternative rendering emphasizing divine splendor |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the Honored One" (EMET/LOGOS). nikhbad means "honored/weighty," not primarily "glorious" (which would be kavod-related).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 11:7 — "see the angels of holiness" vs. "see the holy angels face to face"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "see the-angels of-holiness" | Literal construct chain |
| LOGOS | "behold the holy angels" | Standard English reordering |
| PNEUMA | "see the holy angels face to face" | Added "face to face" for vividness |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "behold the holy angels" (LOGOS). PNEUMA's "face to face" is an addition not supported by the Hebrew text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 11:12 — "Arise, O Hero" vs. "Rise, O Warrior God" — imperative address

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Arise, O-Hero!" | Literal imperative |
| LOGOS | "Arise, O Hero!" | Same, formatted conventionally |
| PNEUMA | "Rise, O Warrior God!" | Interpretive expansion identifying "Hero" as God |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Arise, O Hero!" (EMET/LOGOS). Adding "God" is interpretive; the text uses gibbor alone.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 11:13 — "Worker of valor" vs. "Champion" — divine epithet

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Worker of-valor" | Literal rendering of 'oseh chayil |
| LOGOS | "Doer of Valor" | Formal near-synonym |
| PNEUMA | "Champion" | Single-word dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Worker of valor" (EMET). Closest to the Hebrew; "Champion" (PNEUMA) loses the active participle construction.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 11:15 — "cattle" vs. "livestock" — animal terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "cattle" | Traditional biblical rendering of miqneh |
| LOGOS | "livestock" | Broader English term |
| PNEUMA | "livestock" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "cattle" (EMET). miqneh in biblical context typically rendered "cattle"; maintains traditional register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 11:16 — "rejoice greatly" vs. "rejoice with all your heart" — Zion address

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "rejoice greatly" | Literal rendering echoing Zechariah 9:9 |
| LOGOS | "rejoice exceedingly" | Formal variant |
| PNEUMA | "Rejoice with all your heart" | Dynamic expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "rejoice greatly" (EMET). Echoes Zechariah 9:9 (gili me'od); PNEUMA's "with all your heart" is an interpretive addition.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 11:17 — "perpetually" vs. "continually" vs. "forever" — temporal adverb

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "perpetually" | Rendering of tamid |
| LOGOS | "continually" | Standard alternative for tamid |
| PNEUMA | "forever" | Simplified rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "continually" (LOGOS). Best captures the ongoing, repeated sense of tamid without the finality of "forever."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements:** 15
